findings.issue: wasSanitized forcing attachment regardless of isInlineSafeMime(contentType) result is currently unreachable dead-defense (contentType after sanitization is always "application/octet-stream" when wasSanitized is true, which is not on INLINE_SAFE_IMAGE_SUBTYPES/pdf anyway) — the comment at files.ts:637-641 already acknowledges this explicitly ("it isn't on the allowlist anyway, but this makes the invariant explicit"). Not a defect, just flagging it's belt-and-suspenders on an already-impossible path; fine to keep for future-proofing against an allowlist change that might include octet-stream by accident.
findings.suggestion: No action required — explicit invariant guards against future allowlist changes are reasonable defense-in-depth given this file's own stated discipline (T-0579 precedent).

acceptance_coverage.ac: AC-1: control-byte stored mime → 200 application/octet-stream + attachment, not 500
AC-1b: CRLF header-injection-shaped mime → 200 octet-stream, no injected header reaches the client
AC-2: valid mime (text/plain, image/png+inline) passthrough unchanged after sanitization added
AC-3: XSS-regression — control-byte html-ish mime + ?disposition=inline STILL forced to attachment/octet-stream, never inline
AC-4: over-length (>4096 char) mime → 200 octet-stream, not passed through as-is
